sentences.text: Longusunguis is an extinct enantiornithean dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of Liaoning Province in northeastern China, known for its distinctly elongated foot claws.

This species possesses a unique accessory fenestra on the jugal process of its maxilla, a lateral margin of the coracoid that is more convex than in other bohaiornithids, and an acromion process that projects strongly dorsally.
In this animal, the pygostyle is longer than the tarsometatarsus.

The genus Longusunguis was first described and named by Min Wang, Zhong-He Zhou, Jingmai K. O'Connor, and Nikita V. Zelenkov in 2014, with the species name kurochkini honoring the late paleontologist Evgeny Kurochkin.
It is known only from a single complete and articulated skeleton and skull, the holotype IVPP V 17964, collected near Lamadong Town in Liaoning Province from the Jiufotang Formation.
The holotype specimen represents a subadult individual, indicated by the lack of fusion in compound bones like the carpometacarpus and tarsometatarsus.
Longusunguis lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
